{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Interface Licence Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review findings — TrueLink agreement (Client = Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.)

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. Of 19 rules assessed, **10 are compliant**, **6 are deviations**, **2 clauses are missing**, and **1 requires further verification** before we rely on it.

The commercial risk is concentrated in the risk-allocation provisions. Three findings sit in **walk-away territory** on the playbook's own terms: (i) the Section 8(d) licence permitting TrueLink to distribute, license, resell and exploit our borrowers' Credit Data independently of service delivery; (ii) a liability cap that protects TrueLink only — and is cross-referenced to sections that do not exist in the document — while Client's liability, including its broad indemnity and confidentiality obligations, is entirely unlimited, with no exclusion of indirect or consequential damages anywhere; and (iii) the complete absence of any insurance covenant despite TrueLink hosting the Web Site and processing borrower and loan-applicant data. Section 12's indemnity is also materially one-sided, with no third-party IP infringement indemnity from TrueLink anywhere in the document.

The position is better than expected in several places and we are not redlining them: no exclusivity or non-compete restraint on Client (Section 2(a) expressly preserves our freedom to use alternatives), no liquidated damages or early-termination charge, no non-solicitation covenant, no Vendor audit right, and an MFN that runs **in our favour** under Section 6. Client's unconditional termination election under Section 14 and the one-year term keep the minimum monthly fee floors within the fallback.

Two drafting points to watch as we negotiate: Section 14 is expressed as "Subject to Section 4 hereof" and Section 4 was not in the text supplied — if it contains a minimum-commitment or accelerated-payment mechanic we must revisit the termination and minimum-commitment analysis; and the liability ceiling's cross-reference to "SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11" does not match this document's numbering.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | TrueLink's indemnity (12(b)) covers only its own breach/failure to perform; no third-party IP infringement indemnity anywhere, no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, while Client's indemnity (12(a)) is open-ended. Fails the fallback. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Section 8(d) grants TrueLink a worldwide licence to distribute, license, resell and exploit Credit Data — independent exploitation beyond service delivery (walk-away). Client also has no ownership of or licence to Support Services results (Section 10 makes them confidential only). |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | The only cap protects TrueLink alone and is limited to "SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11" — sections absent from this document. Client's liability is unlimited; no indirect/consequential damages exclusion anywhere. One-way cap with Customer uncapped is walk-away. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Section 15 is the sole assignment provision; no change-of-control language, no successor/M&A carve-out for either party, no notice mechanic and no reasonableness standard on consent. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | "Client" is defined as Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. alone, so the § 2(a) grant does not reach affiliates or contractors; Section 15 bars transfer of the licence to an M&A successor. Both fallback elements fail. |
| High | WARRANTY (medium in list — see note) | — | — | *See row below.* |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation. § 2(a) is non-exclusive and expressly preserves Client's freedom to acquire, develop or licence alternatives; § 3(i) is conditioned on voluntary use of the Interface. At preferred. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination amount. Section 5 minimum monthly amounts are consideration for services provided, not exit sums. At preferred. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint on Client. The § 8(d) "Non-Competition Agreement" reference constrains TrueLink's use of Credit Data and benefits us. At preferred. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Section 14 gives Client an unconditional termination election with run-off to the last day of the following month (~30–60 days), no fee or penalty. No Vendor mid-term convenience right. At or above fallback. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | The only TrueLink warranty (Section 9) is Y2K date-processing; Sections 3 and 4 impose only "reasonable commercial efforts" and Section 2 has no conformance warranty. No warranty period and no repair/replace/refund remedy — fails every fallback element. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Needs review (verification failed)** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Section 13's 30-day non-renewal notice sits inside the 60-day fallback, but Section 6 freezes Hosting Services costs only for one year, leaving renewals repriceable without limit — failing the fallback 5% ceiling. **Proposed insertion did not pass verification; do not issue until re-checked.** |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No exit mechanics. Section 14 sets only the run-off date; Section 13 makes Client responsible for a new name server/hosting environment; Section 10 has no return-or-destroy obligation and Section 24 adds nothing. No data return, export format or deletion obligation anywhere. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No TrueLink right to audit, inspect or verify Client usage, records or systems. § 6 runs the other way, giving Client a documentation and charge-contest right. Better than preferred. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Section 26 selects California law; Section 27 gives exclusive jurisdiction to state/federal courts in San Luis Obispo County. Sits at the fallback (our preference is New York); wording preference only. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No Customer MFN obligation. The only MFN mechanic (§ 6) runs in our favour, capping Hosting Services rates at TrueLink's lowest rate to any other party. At preferred; retained as a benefit. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | Section 5(a) monthly floor fees, but the commitment never extends beyond the current 12-month term, Section 14 allows exit at will with ~a month's notice, and there is no shortfall penalty. Sits at the fallback; floors are unfilled blanks. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicitation or no-hire covenant anywhere; § 8 and § 10 contain none, and the only "unsolicited" reference (§ 7) concerns commercial e-mail. At preferred. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance covenant anywhere in Sections 13–30 or the exhibits (Exhibits A and B are charges only). Given TrueLink hosts the Web Site and processes Credit Data, the absence is walk-away territory. |

*Note on the table: the WARRANTY rule appears once substantively, in the medium-severity block; the placeholder row above is retained only to preserve the severity ordering of the source findings.*

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These three points are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Independent exploitation of Credit Data (IP — § 8 Covenants and Warranties of Client).** The Section 8(d) worldwide licence to distribute, license, resell and exploit our borrowers' Credit Data goes well beyond processing to deliver the services and is not cured by the Section 10 confidentiality provisions. We require the grant to be narrowed to processing solely to provide the Hosting and Support Services.
2. **One-way liability cap with Client uncapped (LOL-CAP — § 12 Indemnity).** The sole ceiling protects TrueLink only, is tied to non-existent sections, and leaves Client's indemnity and confidentiality exposure unlimited with no consequential-damages exclusion. We require a mutual, aggregate cap on the existing 12-month compensation basis, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside it.
3. **No insurance at all (INSURANCE — missing).** With TrueLink hosting the Web Site and transmitting and processing borrower and loan-applicant data, the absence of any insurance covenant is unacceptable. We require a short insurance section at preferred levels, with a cyber trigger broad enough to reach all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client.

The indemnity gap (no third-party IP infringement indemnity from TrueLink anywhere, against an open-ended Client indemnity) is critical and closely linked to items 1 and 2; we would accept the fallback IP-only indemnity with customary exclusions, remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap if TrueLink resists the preferred position.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** on the six deviations and two missing clauses: mutual/aggregate liability cap with carve-outs; TrueLink defence and indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, data breach and wilful misconduct (with notice, defence control and cooperation) and narrowing of Client's indemnity to Client Content and Client's breach of law; narrowed Credit Data licence plus a perpetual licence to Support Services results; asymmetric assignment (Client free to affiliates/successors, TrueLink consent-gated and never to a Client competitor, no termination on Client change of control); licence extension to affiliates on written notice and transfer to an M&A successor; fallback performance warranty (90 days software conformance, 30 days services) with repair, replacement or refund at Client's election in Section 9; a transition assistance and data return clause after Section 14; and an insurance covenant as new Section 31.
2. **Hold the RENEWAL insertion.** That finding did not pass verification. Re-verify the Section 13 notice mechanic and the Section 6 one-year price freeze before we put any renewal-pricing cap language on paper; the substantive concern (unlimited repricing at each renewal) should still be raised commercially.
3. **Obtain the missing text.** Request the full execution version, in particular **Section 4** (Section 14 is "Subject to Section 4") and any section corresponding to the liability cap's reference to "SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11". Our termination-for-convenience and minimum-commitment conclusions are based on the text supplied and would need revisiting if Section 4 contains a minimum-commitment or accelerated-payment mechanic.
4. **Fee negotiation items for the business team** (not legal redlines): the unfilled minimum monthly fee blanks in Section 5(a), the Section 6 bar on contesting the minimum monthly fees, and the apparent mis-citation to "Section 4" where Section 5 is meant. We recommend the renewal price cap be pursued alongside these.
5. **Do not reopen** the compliant items — no exclusivity, no non-compete, no liquidated damages, no non-solicitation, no Vendor audit right, the Vendor-side MFN in Section 6, Section 14 convenience termination, and California law/San Luis Obispo venue. Several of these are better than our preferred position and we should avoid inviting Vendor-favourable additions."}
